chunks: "Because at the same doping level the number of majority carriers is about the same, but electrons are more mobile than holes.
Conductivity is q n micro n for N-type and q p micro p for P-type. With n equals p equals 10 to the 16 per cm³, the only difference is mobility.
Electrons in silicon have about 1350 cm²/V·s and holes about 480, so N-type conducts around 2. 8 times better and its resistivity is about 2. 8 times lower.
As numbers, 10 to the 16 per cm³ doping gives about 0. 5 ohm-centimetres for N-type and about 1. 5 for P-type.

The same ratio shows up in transistors: an N-channel MOSFET has lower on-resistance than a P-channel of the same size, which is why power designers prefer NMOS, and why CMOS needs the PMOS to be wider.
Two caveats. It's at equal doping: if the P-type is doped ten times heavier it will be the better conductor.
And at very heavy doping the gap narrows because impurity scattering dominates both mobilities, to maybe 1. 6x at 10 to the 20 ."
